premise: Fixing the solar panel, Engineer drops her wrench on a rock and waits for the clang — nothing; Pilot presses his helmet to hers so she can hear him laugh.
inspiration: The old riddle of the tree falling where nobody hears it, answered on the Moon, where nobody can.
lesson: Some things are easier to share up close.
learning: Sound can't travel through empty space, so astronauts talk by radio — but touching helmets lets sound through.

en-US.title: The Clang That Never Came
en-US.text: The {solar-panel:enter} solar panel had a {solar-panel:pulse} wobbly bolt. {engineer:enter} Engineer knelt beside it and {engineer:live} gave it three hard turns with her big wrench. Then — oops — the wrench slipped and fell {solar-panel:wobble} onto a rock. {engineer:face surprised} She scrunched her face up for the CLANG. [pause] Nothing. Not a clink. Not a clonk. Even {robot:enter} {robot:face surprised} Robot heard nothing. {sfx:radio} {pilot:enter} {pilot:face happy} Pilot's voice crackled in her helmet. Didn't hear a thing! [laughs] {engineer:face normal} Of course: the Moon has no air, and sound needs air to travel. That's why the crew talk by radio. {pilot:go to engineer} Pilot loped over and pressed his helmet against hers. {sfx:tonk solo} [whispers] Can you hear me now? His voice came through the glass, faint and fuzzy: sound travels through things that touch. {pilot:shake} Then he told her his worst joke. {engineer:face happy} {engineer:shake} She laughed so hard that {solar-panel:live} the solar panel tilted up to see what was so funny.

es-ES.title: El clonc que nunca sonó
es-ES.text: El {solar-panel:enter} panel solar tenía un {solar-panel:pulse} tornillo flojo. {engineer:enter} Ingeniera se arrodilló a su lado y {engineer:live} le dio tres vueltas fuertes con su llave inglesa. Y entonces — ¡uy! — la llave se le escurrió y cayó {solar-panel:wobble} sobre una roca. {engineer:face surprised} Arrugó la cara esperando el ¡CLONC! [pause] Nada. Ni un clinc. Ni un clonc. Ni {robot:enter} {robot:face surprised} Robot oyó nada. {sfx:radio} {pilot:enter} {pilot:face happy} La voz de Piloto chisporroteó en su casco: ¡No he oído nada! [laughs] {engineer:face normal} Claro: en la Luna no hay aire, y el sonido necesita aire para viajar. Por eso la tripulación habla por radio. {pilot:go to engineer} Piloto se acercó y juntó su casco con el de ella. {sfx:tonk solo} [whispers] ¿Me oyes ahora? Su voz cruzó el cristal, bajita: el sonido viaja por las cosas que se tocan. {pilot:shake} Luego le contó su peor chiste. {engineer:face happy} {engineer:shake} Ella se rio tanto que {solar-panel:live} el panel solar se inclinó para ver qué era tan gracioso.

radio.prompt: a short burst of soft radio static and a click, like a walkie-talkie opening, clean and gentle

tonk.prompt: two hard plastic helmets gently bumping together, a soft muffled tonk, close up
